newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $64, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $64, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids early Thursday at $63.00 to $64.00 per cwt were passed by owners pricing remaining cattle at $65.00 following active sales late Wednesday, feedlot sources said.

About 70,000 head sold Wednesday at $64.00, unchanged from last week, in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, they said. Week to date movement in the Panhandle was pegged near 130,000 head, they said.
Kansas feedlots sold about 60,000 head at $64.00 during Wednesday's "fast and furious" trading, one Kansas feedlot manager said. Weekly movement were estimated near 80,000 head.
"I was impressed with the way packers held in there and kept buying cattle instead of pulling out early, which tells me they really needed them," one Panhandle cattle feeder said.
Most showlists were sold out in the Panhandle, but several Kansas feedlot sources said they still had cattle to sell.
Smaller numbers of cattle on this week's showlist, along with higher beef prices up to Wednesday underpinned fed cattle prices, they said.
However, attempts to get $65.00 where thwarted by perceptions that beef prices were near a top and poised to slip, the feedlot sources said.
Boxed beef prices Wednesday were quoted down $0.18 to $0.36 per cwt, with 198 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported. The price decline was the first since July 10, USDA statistics showed.
